# OLIP 0.1 threat model


Status: DRAFT. Written by the sponsor's engineering AI. **Not yet reviewed by an independent security practitioner** (independent review gate not met). Method: STRIDE per asset, with the conformance test that covers each control.

## Assets
A1 CaseBrief content (sensitive personal and legal facts). A2 user contact details. A3 user approval (authorization). A4 handoff payload in transit and at rest. A5 status truth (what really happened). A6 professional identity and license evidence. A7 signing keys. A8 client and recipient credentials. A9 logs and analytics.

## Threats and controls

| # | Threat | Asset | Control in 0.1 | Test | Residual risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Malicious or confused agent approves on the user's behalf | A3 | Approval only via the host's page plus a code to the user's own email; no approve operation for clients; MCP adapter has no approve tool | W4, MCP test | Agent that also controls the user's inbox. Platform-attested approval (0.2) must not weaken this. |
| T2 | Agent forges an authorization id or digest | A3 | Server looks up approvals by id and owner; digest compared and recomputed | W4, W6 | None known |
| T3 | Edit after approval (silent scope change) | A1, A3 | Digest binds revision, recipient, values, purpose, mode, notices; recomputed at submit | W5, W6 | None known |
| T4 | Bulk or unrequested handoffs (spam intake) | A1, A4 | One recipient per preview; user selection flag; single-use approval; rate limits | W3, W12 | Abuse by real users at scale needs per-user limits and abuse review in production |
| T5 | Replay and duplicate delivery | A4 | Idempotency-Key required; per-tenant key store; single-use approval | W7, W20 | Key store must survive restarts in production |
| T6 | Status spoofing ("lawyer confirmed") by agent or tool output | A5 | Recipient events only from authenticated recipient credentials; strict transitions; recipient events and receipts signed (Ed25519); clients verify receipts | W10, W11, W21 | A compromised recipient account can lie; that is the recipient's statement and is labeled as such |
| T7 | Forged tool response claims delivery | A5 | Clients verify receipt signature against the recipient's JWKS and the payload hash | W10 | Clients that skip verification. The MCP adapter returns raw data; a host model can still misreport. |
| T8 | Prompt injection in CaseBrief or profile text | A1, A5 | `content_trust: untrusted_user_supplied`; servers never execute text; state changes only through typed operations | W17 | Downstream LLMs reading payloads must also treat them as data |
| T9 | Cross-tenant leakage | A1, A2 | Owner checks on every object; 404 for others; per-tenant idempotency | W15 | Implementation bugs; needs independent review |
| T10 | Case data in logs or analytics | A9 | Logs: method, route shape, status. Analytics: operation, outcome, coarse codes | W16 | Third-party APM or proxies in production must be configured the same way |
| T11 | Impersonated lawyer or fake firm endpoint | A6 | License evidence levels; jurisdiction + number match; claim and endpoint status separate; recipient keys published per endpoint | R4 | 0.1 has no registry binding a firm's key to its license. Needed before production (O-04). |
| T12 | Overstated verification ("verified lawyer") | A6 | `verification.level` and fixed `display_statement`; indexed must say "not checked" | R4 | Agents may paraphrase; MCP tool text tells them not to |
| T13 | Token theft or long-lived tokens | A8 | 15-minute bearer tokens; client-credentials; constant-time secret compare | W14 | Production should add mTLS or private_key_jwt for clients |
| T14 | Approval-code brute force | A3 | 6 digits, 10-minute expiry, 5 tries, then reset | (manual) | Add per-IP limits in production |
| T15 | Approval page clickjacking or XSS | A3 | CSP `default-src 'none'`, `frame-ancestors` via X-Frame-Options DENY, HTML escaping | (manual) | Needs browser security review |
| T16 | Insecure webhooks / relay transports | A4, A5 | Relay states stop at `sent` without a signed receipt | W9 | Signed webhook spec (O-02) and payload encryption for relays (O-03) not yet defined |
| T17 | Key compromise | A7 | `kid` rotation via JWKS | (none) | Rotation and revocation procedure not yet written |
| T18 | Sensitive document exfiltration | A1 | CaseBrief holds document references only, never content | schema | Document transfer is out of scope in 0.1 |
| T19 | Phishing using OLIP-looking approval pages | A3 | Approval page served from the host's own origin; digest shown | (manual) | User education; domain clearance; the olip.ai domain (registered 2026-11-07); name and trademark clearance not done |
| T20 | Retention beyond what the user expects | A4 | `retention_days` published; delete and export; cancel states limits | W13 | Recipient retention is the recipient's legal obligation, outside OLIP control |

## Incident response (draft)
Severity 1 (unauthorized disclosure of case data or approval bypass): stop write traffic on the affected endpoint within 1 hour by flag, preserve evidence, notify affected users and the recipient as the law requires, publish a post-incident note. An accepted unauthorized disclosure is never "normal" and is counted in the standards scorecard.

## Not covered yet
End-to-end payload encryption, document transfer, key binding to license records, signed webhooks, accessibility review of the approval page, independent penetration test.
